## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--wait` option must be kept as an alias that prints a deprecation warning, as ADR 007 decides. Without it, existing invocations of `--wait` stop working immediately instead of getting the one-release transition the ADR promises.

## Changes
The pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` in `parse_args`, updates the three tests to use `--timeout`, adds ADR 007 describing the transition, and adds a root-level `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Keep `--wait` as an alias with a deprecation warning — When a script passes `--wait 12`, `parse_args` now exits with code 2 and an "unrecognized arguments" error, because line 6 registers only `--timeout`. This contradicts `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." — Every existing caller that uses `--wait` fails as soon as this ships, with no deprecation period and no warning. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` through a custom `argparse.Action` that writes the deprecation warning, and add a `--wait` case to `test_explicit_options`.
